Nagyhalasz Jewish Cemetery Two

Jewish Cemetery · Nagyhalász, Hungary

Not demolished. The second of two Jewish cemeteries in Nagyhalász also appears on an 1870 cadastral map, though its current condition is unconfirmed - the site could not be directly accessed for a full survey. It served the same community as the town's other cemetery: growing from 75 residents in 1848 to a peak of 312 by 1930, with a formally organized congregation from 1881 that maintained a burial society, mikveh, school, and yeshiva. By 1944 its Orthodox community numbered 262 before deportation to Auschwitz via Nyíregyháza; roughly 40 survived, and the community had shrunk to just 3 Jews by 1963.
